description: A template for concept analysis using Rodgers' (2000) evolutionary method. Includes the standard six elements plus a customisable analytical framework section. Modify the 'Your Analytical Framework' group to fit your research questions.
method_reference: Rodgers, B.L. (2000). Concept analysis: An evolutionary view. In B.L. Rodgers & K.A. Knafl (Eds.), Concept Development in Nursing (2nd ed., pp. 77-102). Philadelphia: Saunders.

fields.label: Author(s)
fields.help_text: Last name, initials. Multiple authors separated by semicolons.

fields.label: Author Discipline
fields.help_text: Primary discipline of the first or corresponding author.

field_groups.description: Core extraction fields from Rodgers' evolutionary method. Extract direct quotes with page numbers where relevant.

fields.label: Attributes
fields.help_text: Defining characteristics of the concept as described or implied in this source. What IS the concept according to this author?

fields.label: Antecedents
fields.help_text: What precedes or gives rise to the concept? What conditions, contexts, or events lead to it?

fields.label: Consequences
fields.help_text: What follows from the concept? What outcomes, responses, or effects are described?

fields.label: Surrogate Terms
fields.help_text: Terms used interchangeably with or instead of the concept. Note the term AND the context of use.

fields.label: Related Concepts
fields.help_text: Concepts that are connected to but distinct from the target concept. Note how the source distinguishes or conflates them.

fields.label: Context / References
fields.help_text: The disciplinary, cultural, legal, and temporal context. How does context shape the way this source constructs the concept?

field_groups.description: Customise this section for your research questions. The example fields below are placeholders to demonstrate different field types.

fields.label: Primary Theme
fields.help_text: Replace these with your own themes or analytical categories.

fields.label: Tags

options.label: Example Tag 1
options.description: Replace with your own tag and description.

options.label: Example Tag 2
options.description: Multi-select fields let you code sources across multiple categories.

options.label: Example Tag 3
options.description: Great for tracking which research questions each source speaks to.

fields.help_text: Select all that apply. Customise these in schemas.js to match your analytical framework.

fields.label: Example Flag
fields.help_text: Boolean fields are useful for flagging sources that do something specific (e.g., conflates two concepts, uses a particular methodology).

field_groups.description: Your interpretive work. This is where the analysis lives.

fields.label: Analytic Memo
fields.help_text: Your thinking about this source. What surprised you? What contradictions do you notice? How does this connect to other sources? There are no wrong answers. This is your researcher voice.

fields.label: Key Quotes
fields.help_text: Direct quotes with page numbers that capture something essential about how this source constructs the concept.

fields.label: Source Quality Notes
fields.help_text: Any notes on methodological quality, limitations, or biases.
